scenes.visual: Title card 'Different Cells, Shared DNA'. Reuse the first film's colour map exactly: movement BLUE, feeding GOLD, water balance TEAL, reproduction GREEN, nerve signalling VIOLET, oxygen carrying RED, shared DNA MAGENTA, tissues and organs ORANGE. New neutral cell outlines are CREAM. Flat cell cartoons are labelled 'schematic' and are not to scale.

scenes.tts: The first film showed how many-celled organisms share life's jobs. How can their cells become different enough to do those jobs?
scenes.visual: The first film's cluster returns with BLUE, GOLD, TEAL, and GREEN job tokens in different cells. The cells still have identical round outlines. A question mark stretches those outlines into faint possible shapes.
scenes.narration: The first film showed how many-celled organisms share life's jobs. How can their cells become different enough to do those jobs?

scenes.tts: A specialized cell has a structure suited to a particular job. Form is not decoration. It changes what the cell can reach, carry, or move.
scenes.visual: One large CREAM cell fills the frame. Its outline smoothly stretches, flattens, and bends while three action arrows appear: reach, carry, move. The label 'specialized: fitted for a job' stays fixed.
scenes.narration: A specialized cell has a structure suited to a particular job. Form is not decoration. It changes what the cell can reach, carry, or move.

scenes.tts: A neuron grows a long, thin axon. It can carry a signal from the spine to the foot. Its reach fits long-distance signalling.
scenes.visual: The same CREAM cell stretches one extension across most of the frame and becomes a schematic neuron. A VIOLET pulse travels along the axon from a labelled spine outline toward a labelled foot silhouette.
scenes.narration: A neuron grows a long, thin axon. It can carry a signal from the spine to the foot. Its reach fits long-distance signalling.

scenes.tts: A skeletal muscle cell is a long cylinder packed with fibres that shorten together. A root hair cell grows a thin tube into soil, adding contact where water enters.
scenes.visual: The neuron transforms into an ORANGE-striped muscle cylinder. Its fibres slide and shorten the cell. It then transforms into a plant root-surface cell whose long TEAL tube threads between soil particles as water arrows enter.
scenes.narration: A skeletal muscle cell is a long cylinder packed with fibres that shorten together. A root hair cell grows a thin tube into soil, adding contact where water enters.

scenes.tts: Structure can affect survival. In Arabidopsis seedlings, lines with longer root hairs stayed anchored better after simulated rain. Their main roots were about the same size. So root hair length is the likely reason.
scenes.visual: Two schematic Arabidopsis seedlings with equal-length main roots sit in a tilted soil box. Longer TEAL root hairs grip more soil as animated rain passes; the short-haired seedling shifts. Labels say 'main roots: about the same size' and 'root hairs differ'.
scenes.narration: Structure can affect survival. In Arabidopsis seedlings, lines with longer root hairs stayed anchored better after simulated rain. Their main roots were about the same size. So root hair length is the likely reason.

scenes.tts: Now compare two red blood cell cartoons. One is a stiff sphere. The other is a flexible disc dented in the middle. Which passes a narrow vessel?
scenes.visual: Two CREAM red-cell cartoons approach identical narrow vessel openings. Left is labelled 'stiff sphere, schematic'; right is labelled 'flexible dented disc, schematic'. Both pause at the entrance beneath the question.
scenes.narration: Now compare two red blood cell cartoons. One is a stiff sphere. The other is a flexible disc dented in the middle. Which passes a narrow vessel?

scenes.visual: Predict pause. Both cell cartoons wait at the vessel openings while a five-second ring timer fills.

scenes.tts: The flexible dented disc bends and squeezes through. A mature red blood cell also has no nucleus. Its small flexible form suits transport through narrow vessels.
scenes.visual: The stiff sphere stops at the opening. The dented disc folds, passes through, and springs back. A nucleus icon fades out only from the mature red cell, and the vessel carries it onward.
scenes.narration: The flexible dented disc bends and squeezes through. A mature red blood cell also has no nucleus. Its small flexible form suits transport through narrow vessels.

scenes.tts: Different shapes raise a deeper question. Do nerve and muscle cells carry different instructions? Mostly no. Nearly every body cell with a nucleus carries essentially the same D N A.
scenes.caption: Different shapes raise a deeper question. Do nerve and muscle cells carry different instructions? Mostly no. Nearly every body cell with a nucleus carries essentially the same DNA.
scenes.visual: The neuron and muscle cell return side by side. Each nucleus opens to show the same MAGENTA strip of labelled gene blocks in the same order. A large 'same DNA' bracket joins the strips.
scenes.narration: Different shapes raise a deeper question. Do nerve and muscle cells carry different instructions? Mostly no. Nearly every body cell with a nucleus carries essentially the same DNA.

scenes.tts: What differs is gene expression, the use of a gene's instructions to make a product. Each kind of cell uses a different set of genes. Cells fit life's jobs through structure and gene use, alone or together.
scenes.visual: On both MAGENTA DNA strips, shared background blocks glow softly. In the muscle cell, blocks labelled 'shortening proteins' brighten ORANGE. In the neuron, a different set brightens VIOLET. Products move outward and reshape each cell.
scenes.narration: What differs is gene expression, the use of a gene's instructions to make a product. Each kind of cell uses a different set of genes. Cells fit life's jobs through structure and gene use, alone or together.

scenes.tts: A muscle cell uses genes for proteins that slide and shorten it. Other genes stay unused.
scenes.visual: The ORANGE muscle-gene block sends plain protein bars into sliding fibres, which shorten. Unused blocks on the MAGENTA strip remain dim, not deleted.
scenes.narration: A muscle cell uses genes for proteins that slide and shorten it. Other genes stay unused.

scenes.tts: A developing red blood cell uses genes for hemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen. Later it pushes out its nucleus. Its earlier gene use helped build its specialized contents.
scenes.visual: A nucleated developing red cell's MAGENTA DNA strip lights one block labelled 'hemoglobin' in RED. Plain RED cargo dots fill the cell without any molecular structure. The nucleus then moves to the edge and exits as the cell matures.
scenes.narration: A developing red blood cell uses genes for hemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen. Later it pushes out its nucleus. Its earlier gene use helped build its specialized contents.

scenes.tts: This is a main model, not a claim without exceptions. Some immune cells rearrange D N A. Egg and sperm cells carry one chromosome set, while most body cells carry two.
scenes.caption: This is a main model, not a claim without exceptions. Some immune cells rearrange DNA. Egg and sperm cells carry one chromosome set, while most body cells carry two.
scenes.visual: The same-DNA bracket stays central but gains a label 'main model: nucleated body cells'. Beside it, small exception cards slide in: 'some immune cells: DNA rearranged', 'egg and sperm: one set', 'most body cells: two sets'.
scenes.narration: This is a main model, not a claim without exceptions. Some immune cells rearrange DNA. Egg and sperm cells carry one chromosome set, while most body cells carry two.

scenes.tts: Experiments support the model. A few frog gut-cell nuclei, moved into eggs, still built tadpoles with nerve, muscle, and blood cells. In those nuclei, specializing had not thrown the unused genes away.
scenes.visual: A MAGENTA nucleus moves from a schematic frog gut cell into an egg whose own nucleus is crossed out. Most of a row of such eggs fade as failures; one develops into a small tadpole silhouette, with VIOLET nerve, ORANGE muscle, and RED blood-cell icons. Label 'a few transfers succeeded; most failed'.
scenes.narration: Experiments support the model. A few frog gut-cell nuclei, moved into eggs, still built tadpoles with nerve, muscle, and blood cells. In those nuclei, specializing had not thrown the unused genes away.

scenes.tts: So cell differences need not mean different instruction books. Different cells use different parts of a shared book, building structures that suit their work.
scenes.visual: The identical MAGENTA strips close like shared instruction books. Different coloured tabs open in neuron, muscle, red blood, and root hair cells. Each cell performs its carried action around a common centre.
scenes.narration: So cell differences need not mean different instruction books. Different cells use different parts of a shared book, building structures that suit their work.

scenes.visual: End card shows one line only: 'Cells fit life's jobs through structure and gene use, alone or together.'
